cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Which quantity is NOT a state function?

questions.stem: Which of the following is a state function?
options: The path taken between two states
questions.explanation: Entropy depends only on the state. Heat and work depend on the path, and the path itself is not a property of a state. The other choices fail because each describes a quantity tied to how the change happened.
questions.subtopic: Systems, state functions and process types

questions.stem: During the boiling of water at 1 atm, the heat supplied
options: Raises the temperature of the liquid
Increases potential energy while T stays constant
Raises the average kinetic energy of the molecules
Lowers the vapor pressure of the liquid
questions.explanation: At the plateau, energy overcomes intermolecular attractions. T and average KE stay constant, and vapor pressure equals the external pressure.

questions.stem: For a spontaneous process, ΔS(system) = -40 J/K. This is possible if
questions.explanation: The second law needs ΔS(universe) > 0. A system can lose entropy when the surroundings gain more. In an isolated system ΔS(sys) itself must be positive.

questions.stem: A reaction has k = 4.0 x 10^-3 s^-1. The overall order is
questions.explanation: A unit of s^-1 is the signature of first order, because rate (M/s) = k[A] requires k in s^-1. Zero order would need M/s, second order M^-1 s^-1, and third order M^-2 s^-1.

questions.stem: Which conditions favor the thermodynamic product?
options: Low temperature and short time under irreversible conditions
Higher temperature and long reaction time under reversible conditions
Low temperature with a strong catalyst only
Short reaction time at any temperature
questions.explanation: Equilibration lets material funnel to the most stable product. Low T, short time, and irreversibility lock in the kinetic product.

demo_cards.front: Define a system and its surroundings in thermodynamics.
demo_cards.back: The system is the part of the universe under study. Everything else is the surroundings. System plus surroundings is the universe.

demo_cards.text: A {{c1::state function}} depends only on the initial and final states. Examples: {{c2::U, H, S, G, T, P, V}}.
demo_cards.extra: Path-independent. A change in a state function is just final minus initial.

demo_cards.stem: Which quantity is NOT a state function?
demo_cards.why: Work depends on the path. U, S, and G depend only on the state.

demo_cards.statement: Heat is a state function because energy is conserved.
demo_cards.why: Heat is a path function. Conservation links q and w to the state function U, but q alone depends on the route.
